songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World
It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: Blues‑laden early Dead set with fiery Pigpen and sharp Garcia
ai_show_review.blurb: An energetic blues‑focused set showcases Pigpen’s raw vocals on numbers like “Next Time You See Me” and “One Kind Favor.” Jerry Garcia adds standout guitar licks and vocal moments, while Phil provides a solid driving bass despite occasional choppiness. The best source is the good‑quality field recording that preserves most of the performance.
ai_show_review.review:
On March 12, 1966 at the Danish Center in Los Angeles the Grateful Dead delivered a raw, blues‑heavy Acid Test set that still crackles with early‑Dead energy. Pigpen dominates the vocal front‑line, belting his soulful harmonica‑infused renditions of “Next Time You See Me,” “One Kind Favor / See My Grave Is Kept Clean,” and “It’s A Sin,” while Jerry Garcia throws in scorching licks – even mimicking a horn line on “Midnight Hour” in one version – and steps up to the mic on “Hey Little One.” Phil Lesh underpins the band with a driving, if occasionally choppy, bass foundation, and Bob Weir adds rhythm guitar and nascent lead work that shines despite being buried in some mixes. The set flows through traditional blues numbers and early originals, keeping the energy high from start to finish.

Four recordings of this show exist, ranging from an audience tape with a surf‑y, over‑present guitar to two soundboard captures plagued by pitch quirks and low drum levels. The most listenable source is the good‑quality field recording (gd66‑acid‑test‑supplement.sbd.unknown.9514.shnf), which despite some hiss offers a tight, balanced picture of the full set and lets Pigpen’s vocals and Garcia’s guitar shine. For anyone interested in hearing the Dead at the cusp of their psychedelic transformation, this show is a must‑listen – especially for its blistering blues moments and early signs of the improvisational fire that would later define them.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality field recording that captures the full set with tight, listenable sound and minimal dropouts, showcasing Pigpen’s vocals and Garcia’s guitar clearly.

key_highlights: Blues‑heavy set dominated by Pigpen’s powerhouse vocals.
Jerry Garcia delivers scorching early solos and strong vocal moments.
The field recording provides surprisingly clear audio for a 1966 archival tape.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is front‑and‑center, delivering scorching licks early in the set and strong vocal deliveries on “It’s A Sin” and “Hey Little One,” though on some tapes his tone leans surfy.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass provides a solid, driving foundation despite occasional choppiness and muffling on lower‑quality recordings.
band_performance.Bob: Weir contributes steady rhythm guitar and adds vocal harmonies, with notable singing on “Beat It On Down The Line” and early lead work on “One Kind Favor,” though often buried in the mix.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is generally tight, but some recordings render his kit very low or even inaudible.
